source.author: verg
source.text: Hic tamen hanc mecum poteras requiescere noctem fronde super viridi: sunt nobis mitia poma, castaneae molles, et pressi copia lactis; et iam summa procul villarum culmina fumant, maioresque cadunt altis de montibus umbrae.
source.text_original: Hic tamen hanc mecum poteras requiescere noctem / fronde super viridi: sunt nobis mitia poma, / castaneae molles, et pressi copia lactis; / et iam summa procul villarum culmina fumant, / maioresque cadunt altis de montibus umbrae.
source.text_english: Yet here you could have spent this night with me, on a bed of green leaves: we have ripe fruit, soft chestnuts, and an abundance of pressed milk; and now the roofs of the farms are smoking far off, and the shadows fall longer from the high mountains.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Secundum illud Virgilianum: Et jam summa procul villarum culmina fumant: Majoresque cadunt altis de montibus umbrae.
reuse.text_original: Secundum illud Virgilianum: Et jam summa procul villarum culmina fumant: Majoresque cadunt altis de montibus umbrae.
reuse.text_english: According to that line of Virgil: And now the highest roofs of the villas smoke in the distance, and the longer shadows fall from the lofty mountains.
